The wealth gap in Germany is a pressing issue that demands attention and action from our government. For too long, the wealthy 10% have held over 60% of total net wealth, while the bottom 50% hold less than 3%. This is a stark reminder that our tax system is not working as it should. We must address this imbalance and create a more just and equitable society, where everyone contributes their fair share.

As Social Democrats, we believe that a wealth tax is a necessary step towards achieving this goal. By taxing wealth, we can redistribute wealth and create a more level playing field. This is not about stifling economic growth, as some have suggested, but about ensuring that everyone contributes their fair share. We must also reform the inheritance tax, which currently favors large business fortunes over smaller family-owned businesses. This is not only unfair but also undermines social cohesion.

Our proposal for a wealth tax is designed to be fair and efficient. We will make sure that the circle of those affected is not expanded and that no more citizens have to pay the solidarity surcharge than today. We want to ensure that high-net-worth individuals contribute a fair share to the financing of our future investments. This will not only reduce inequality but also create a more stable and sustainable economic environment.

In contrast, the opposition's approach of cutting red tape and reducing taxes may sound appealing, but it is a recipe for disaster. It will only widen the wealth gap and create more inequality. We cannot afford to repeat the mistakes of the past, when the wealthy few benefited at the expense of the many. It's time for a new approach, one that puts the needs of all Germans, not just the wealthy few, at the forefront.
